summary: Catalogue-wide screen of Modular Curves (Katz–Mazur) against all 212 other roadmaps: the 211 other atlas roadmaps and the new MordellLawrenceVenkatesh. The focal document and every stage were read in full. Named suppliers and every roadmap citing '#81', 'PR81' or the Katz–Mazur roadmap were read in full or stage by stage; the rest were screened by summary and stage keywords. 46 links (42 explicit, 4 inferred). 14 run into Modular Curves: JacobianChallenge A–C into 0A, 1C, 2D and Layer 10; EllipticCurves L1–L2 into 2A, 2E and Layer 10; AlgebraicCurves L7–L9 and L12 into Layer 10. 32 run out of it, mainly to ModularCurvesPartII (13), AbelianSchemes (5), ShimuraVarieties (3) and MordellLawrenceVenkatesh (2), plus one each to AlgebraicModuli, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations, EllipticCurveModularity, FiniteFlatGroups, PELModuli, PerfectoidShimuraVarieties, ShimuraCompactifications, HeegnerPointEulerSystems and KatoEulerSystems. 19 overlaps: 14 rescope and 5 keep, none merge. overlaps.detail: Jacobian Challenge Layer D defines, for X → Spec k, the fppf Picard functor T ↦ Pic(X_T)/Pic(T), its rigidification by a section with a Poincaré bundle, and Pic⁰ as the degree-zero subfunctor. Modular Curves 2D defines the same functor, rigidified functor, degree-zero subfunctor and normalized Poincaré bundle for E/S over an arbitrary base, and proves representability by E. JC's genus-one acceptance check Jac(E, O) ≅ E is the case S = Spec k of 2D's λ_E.
overlaps.proposal: State the Picard functor, its rigidified form and the degree-zero subfunctor once, over an arbitrary base S, in JC Layer D; none of these definitions needs a field. 2D imports them and keeps representability by E, the normalized Poincaré bundle with its biextension identities, and λ_E : E ≅ Pic⁰_{E/S} with its t_{-P}^* sign convention. JC's genus-one check is then λ_E specialised to S = Spec k, with the sign matched to JC's Abel–Jacobi map x ↦ 𝒪(x − x₀).

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 7E (PD-2, PD-3) defines ordinary and supersingular for E₀/k through the connected–étale structure of E₀[p] (EllipticCurve.IsSupersingular). It also constructs relative Frobenius and Verschiebung with V∘F = p = F∘V over bases of characteristic p. Elliptic Curves Layer 3 defines IsSupersingular by E[p](K^sep) = O, and Layer 1 constructs the Frobenius twist, relative Frobenius and Verschiebung with V∘F = [p]. So the same predicates and isogenies are built twice, once on schemes and once on equations, and no comparison is stated between them.
overlaps.proposal: Keep both; the boundary between scheme-level and equation-level theory is deliberate. Beside 7E's existing bridges for deg [N] and the Weil pairing, add comparison lemmas over a field for elliptic W. First, IsSupersingular for projModel W agrees with Elliptic Curves' IsSupersingular. Second, the scheme Frobenius and Verschiebung of projModel W match the equation-level maps under 2A's function-field identification.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 7C constructs the formal group Ê of an elliptic curve over a complete local ring, the parameter X with completed local ring A[[X]], coordinate changes X ↦ uX + ⋯ and the p-series; 8C uses the series [a](X). Elliptic Curves Layer 1 constructs the elliptic formal group law Ê over the coefficient ring, as an instance of Mathlib's RingTheory/FormalGroup, with [m] on Ê. Over a local base E has a global Weierstrass model, so both describe the same formal group law in the parameter z = −x/y.
overlaps.proposal: Keep 7C's intrinsic construction, which does not depend on a parameter, and its compatibility with the scheme group law. Identify its expression in the Weierstrass parameter with Elliptic Curves Layer 1's formal group law instead of recomputing the power series, and take 8C's [a](X) from EC's [m] on Ê. 7G's formal engine already uses Mathlib's FormalGroup carrier, so the carriers agree.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves Layer 10 builds the Tate curve over ℤ[1/N]((q)) with T[N], its [Γ₀(N)]-structures and formal cusp parameters (KM 8.7–8.11, 10.8). Elliptic Curves Layer 4 defines the Tate-curve coefficients a₄ and a₆ as q-series over ℤ⟦q⟧, proves the divisibility by 12, and gives Δ(q) and j(q) = 1/q + 744 + ⋯ before specialising to complete fields. The integral Weierstrass equation over ℤ⟦q⟧ and its Δ and j identities belong to both. Modular Curves states that EC's uniformisation L^×/q^ℤ ≅ E_q(L) is not a supplier, which is correct for the uniformisation itself.
overlaps.proposal: Elliptic Curves Layer 4 exports, as its own milestone before any valued-field specialisation, the Weierstrass curve E_q over ℤ⟦q⟧ with its a₄, a₆, Δ(q) and j(q) theorems. Modular Curves Layer 10 base-changes that curve to ℤ[1/N]((q)) and keeps T[N], the level structures, the integral closures and the formal cusp parameters. The uniformisation stays in Elliptic Curves.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 2A proves three things: K(projModel W) ≃ W.toAffine.FunctionField; morphisms from an integral scheme to a separated target that agree at the generic point are equal; and a nonconstant finite morphism of smooth projective integral curves over a field is finite flat, with fibre length equal to the function-field degree. Algebraic Curves Layer 12 (12B–12D) proves the general normalisation, generic-point and anti-equivalence statements, and names isogenies of W.FunctionField as its acceptance instance. 2A is the elliptic special case, kept narrow on purpose.
overlaps.proposal: Keep 2A's narrow bridge so that Modular Curves does not wait for Algebraic Curves' final layer. Once 12C exists, add a compatibility lemma identifying projModelFunctionFieldEquiv and the generic-point extensionality lemma with AC's model functor on W.FunctionField. Do not extend 2A into the general comparison for arbitrary isogenies.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves Layer 10 builds the formal-cusp package: the Tate curve over ℤ[1/N]((q)) with T[N] and [Γ₀(N)]-structures, the integral closure of the q-adic local ring, formal parameters, cusp widths 1 and N, and the cusp count as orbits of KM 10.6 cusp labels. It separates the non-reduced cusp fibre, its reduced locus and its Cartier structure, and handles ramification and stabilisers in characteristics 2 and 3. ModularCurvesPartII R13.3 extends the Tate curve to generalised elliptic curves, computes completed local rings and cusp widths, and records ramification and stabilisers in characteristics 2 and 3. It separates the same three cusp-fibre assertions. On the prime-level diamond class over ℤ[1/N] both compute the same objects.
overlaps.proposal: R13.3 imports Layer 10's formal-cusp package on that class (N ≥ 5 prime, H ≤ (ℤ/Nℤ)ˣ/{±1}, over ℤ[1/N]), as R12.3 already does for the compactification. It adds only the boundary data of generalised elliptic curves, composite and small levels, and primes dividing the level. Prove that the formal parameters agree where both are defined; do not recompute Layer 10's cusp widths or its table of stabilisers in characteristics 2 and 3.

overlaps.detail: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3 constructs fppf quotients of abelian schemes by finite locally free subgroups, and isogenies with their duals. It shows that [n] is finite locally free of rank n^{2g}, étale when n is invertible, and builds the Weil pairing A[n] × A∨[n] from Cartier duality. In relative dimension one these are Modular Curves 2B (E/C), 2A (E[N] of rank N²) and 2E (the Cartier–Nishi pairing and e_N). A1 and A2 require comparisons with #81's elliptic curves and Picard/Poincaré construction; A3 states none.
overlaps.proposal: Keep both: the genus-one routes in Modular Curves are upstream and specific. Add genus-one comparison lemmas to A3, as A1 and A2 already have. A/C should agree with 2B's E/C, and the rank-n^{2g} theorem should specialise to 2A. The pairing A[n] × A∨[n] composed with λ_E should agree with 2E's e_N, with the sign fixed. The roadmap's completion test, which compares elliptic Weil pairings through both APIs, then becomes a theorem.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 7F ST-1 formalises the Serre–Tate equivalence: deformations of E₀ over artinian local W(k)-algebras are equivalent to deformations of E₀[p^∞]. Its source, Katz's Serre–Tate local moduli, Theorem 1.2.1, is stated for abelian schemes. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 proves the Serre–Tate equivalence for abelian schemes with endomorphism and polarization structures. The same theorem is planned twice.
overlaps.proposal: Split A4. An early part proves Katz's Theorem 1.2.1 for abelian schemes over artinian local rings in which p is nilpotent, using only A1 and p-divisible groups. A later part adds endomorphism and polarization structures and the tangent comparison via Grothendieck–Messing. 7F's ST-1 then specialises the early part to elliptic curves through A1. ST-2 to ST-5 stay in 7F: the supersingular universal deformation, the two local models, pro-representability with level structure, and the parameter criterion. If 7F lands first, it proves the elliptic case, and the early A4 part generalises it with a comparison lemma rather than a second proof.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 0G constructs the relative Grassmannian of locally free rank-N quotients (affine charts, transition maps, gluing, universal property). It then cuts out Hopf-ideal loci to get the parameter scheme of rank-N subgroup schemes. 0F represents Weil restriction of affine finitely presented X → Z along finite locally free Z → S by an affine scheme. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.1 constructs Grassmannians with their universal properties, and its handoff lists the chart equations, universal quotient, flattening locus and gluing. R09.3 owns Weil restriction along finite locally free bases as an algebraic space (Stacks 05YC/05YF). Both roadmaps claim the relative Grassmannian scheme and Weil restriction.
overlaps.proposal: Build the relative Grassmannian once. AM's summary says to 'Reassign any item already claimed by a live supplier rather than duplicate it', so AM R09.1 should import MC 0G's relative Grassmannian and universal quotient. AM then adds projective bundles, flag schemes, Hilbert polynomials and boundedness. MC 0G keeps the Hopf-ideal equations and the parameter scheme of subgroup schemes. AM R09.3 states its algebraic-space Weil restriction as an extension of MC 0F's affine case, with a comparison lemma.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 0E proves effective faithfully flat descent for many objects: affine and finite locally free schemes, closed subschemes, sections and morphisms, projective relative curves with a descended relatively ample line bundle, group objects and group laws, subgroups, level structures and torsors. It forbids effective descent for projective schemes without descended polarisation data. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.3 proves effective descent for 'the sheaves, finite flat groups, polarisations and projective objects', separating descent of a line bundle from descent of an object equipped with one. SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1 proves effective fpqc/fppf descent 'for the required objects'. StableReduction Layer 2 builds effective étale descent for schemes with a compatible relatively ample invertible sheaf, via the graded section algebra and relative Proj, and forbids descent without a polarisation. Four roadmaps plan the same polarised effective descent.
overlaps.proposal: Prove one general theorem: effective fpqc descent for schemes projective over the base together with a descended relatively ample invertible sheaf, including morphisms, sections, group structures and closed subschemes. Its natural home is SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1, whose summary says to adopt existing owners. MC 0E and SR Layer 2 then keep only their instances (relative curves, level structures and torsors; contraction descent). Until SF.1 exists, MC 0E is the live supplier: generalise its polarised case from relative curves to projective S-schemes so that AM R09.3 and SR Layer 2 can import it instead of proving it again.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 9D constructs coarse moduli schemes M(𝒫) of affine moduli problems over Ell. It takes quotients 𝕄(𝒫,δ)/G by Galois rigidifiers ([Γ(3)] on D(3), [Γ(4)] on D(2)), glues them, proves the classifying map and the bijection on field points, and proves KM 8.1.5–8.1.6 on quotients and base change; 9E adds the coarse j-line. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.5 proves that coarse spaces exist for the finite-inertia and quotient presentations used in the programme, with exact base-change statements. It also adds or removes auxiliary level prime to the characteristic to rigidify automorphisms. Its required checks compare the coarse j-line with the moduli stack of elliptic curves. For elliptic moduli problems these are the same constructions.
overlaps.proposal: AM R09.5 keeps the general coarse-space theorem for stacks with finite inertia (generalised elliptic curves, abelian schemes). It proves that on Modular Curves' affine problems over Ell this recovers 9D's M(𝒫) and its base-change statements, rather than rebuilding auxiliary-level rigidification for elliptic curves. Its check on the coarse j-line should use 9E's coarseJLine_int.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 7B identifies the completed strict-henselian local ring of a rigidified finite moduli scheme at a geometric point with the ring pro-representing the marked deformation groupoid, functorially in the rigidifier. 7D compares the universal deformation over W(k)[[T]] with completed local rings of representing moduli schemes. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.6 relates the deformation functor at a geometric point to the completed local ring of the constructed scheme or stack, including stabilisers and versality. 7B and 7D are the elliptic case.
overlaps.proposal: Keep 7B and 7D as the concrete Katz–Mazur statements; they work with rigidified finite schemes, not stacks. When R09.6 exists, add a lemma showing that it specialises to 7B on rigidified elliptic moduli problems. Use 7B and 7D as R09.6's elliptic acceptance test instead of proving the elliptic case a second time.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 0B builds, over any base, the category of finite locally free commutative group schemes. It covers kernels with base change, fppf quotients by closed finite locally free subgroups with fppf exactness, and constant and diagonalizable group schemes. It also covers Cartier duality (biduality, rank, base change, exactness, (ℤ/N)^D ≅ μ_N) and the theorem that a group of rank N is killed by N; 0C supplies torsor and equivalence-relation quotients. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 develops Cartier duality, finite-flat subgroup and quotient constructions, and fpqc descent. Its document calls FFG 'the sole owner of dimension-general finite flat commutative group schemes, Cartier duality and Barsotti–Tate groups'. The same document also says that #81 owns the elliptic subgroup and pairing theory and that FFG extends that work. Ownership of general Cartier duality therefore conflicts.
overlaps.proposal: Make MC 0B and 0C the owners of the base-general category, kernels, fppf quotients and Cartier duality. They are upstream, already stated over arbitrary bases, and consumed by 2E. FFG R07.1 imports them and owns what is new: connected–étale sequences over its allowed bases, generic and special fibres, finite-flat closure, Raynaud's theorem, and p-divisible groups and Tate modules over local bases. Correct FFG's 'sole owner' sentence. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3's 'generic finite-group-scheme supplier' then means MC 0B/0C together with R07.1's additions.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 7E schedules a short list of p-divisible-group statements. PD-1 is the tower E[p^∞] with PDivisibleGroupIso. PD-2 is the connected–étale sequence of finite locally free commutative group schemes over henselian local rings, with the ordinary/supersingular dichotomy. PD-3 is Frobenius and Verschiebung. PD-5 classifies E₀[p^∞] over an algebraically closed field using Lazard's height classification, and Dieudonné theory is explicitly excluded. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 defines p-divisible groups and connected–étale sequences in general. R07.2 proves the Dieudonné classification, including Frobenius and Verschiebung and the ordinary and supersingular cases.
overlaps.proposal: Keep 7E's list scoped to Katz–Mazur, so that Modular Curves does not wait for Dieudonné theory. FFG R07.1 defines p-divisible groups compatibly with PD-1's PDivisibleGroupIso and states PD-2 at full generality, importing it where the hypotheses match rather than reproving it. R07.2 proves that its ordinary and supersingular cases agree with PD-2 and PD-5 for elliptic curves.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 0B develops, over an arbitrary base S, the anti-equivalence between affine group schemes and Hopf algebras. It draws on Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Affine.lean, which its document says is present at its Mathlib pin. 0B also builds scheme-theoretic kernels, fppf quotients, D_S(M) with μ_N = D_S(ℤ/Nℤ), and Cartier duality. ReductiveGroups Layer 0 plans to build the same anti-equivalence; its inventory says that 'the Toric work ... is not in master'. Its Layer 3 covers Hopf ideals, kernels and fppf quotients, and Layer 4 covers D(M) and μ_n = D(ℤ/n). Layer 4 calls Cartier duality 'a related but distinct statement to develop separately'. ReductiveGroups works over a field first.
overlaps.proposal: Both roadmaps consume Mathlib's Group/Affine.lean anti-equivalence. ReductiveGroups Layer 0 records that it has landed and keeps only the functor of points with its convolution structure and the three-way dictionary. Build D_S(M), μ_N, and kernels and fppf quotients by finite locally free subgroups once, over an arbitrary base, in MC 0B. RG Layers 3–4 specialise these to S = Spec k and keep the reductive quotients (Matsushima) and tori. The Cartier duality that RG says to 'develop separately' is MC 0B's.

overlaps.detail: EllipticKTheory E.1 constructs, for an elliptic Weierstrass equation over a field, the smooth projective scheme with its section at infinity. It proves smoothness and properness and identifies the function field. It compares F-points and the group law with Mathlib's point group, and compares function-field isogenies with scheme morphisms. Modular Curves already supplies most of this. 1A gives the scheme model over any ring, with properness, smoothness and base change. 1B gives the dictionary for field points, and 1D the agreement of the group law with Mathlib's on field-valued fibres. 2A gives the function-field identification and the bridge for [N].
overlaps.proposal: E.1 imports 1A, 1B, 1D and 2A, base-changed to a field. It adds only what is missing: geometric connectedness and regularity where needed, pullbacks of divisors, and the comparison for arbitrary isogenies. That comparison should come from AlgebraicCurves Layer 12C, which owns it. Delete E.1's claim that 'E supplies the elliptic scheme specialisation'.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 0D constructs, over a field K, the equivalence between finite étale K-schemes and finite continuous Gal(K^s/K)-sets. It proves that the equivalence preserves products and transports group objects, commutative group objects, homomorphisms and alternating pairings, as 5C needs for V_ρ. InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.0 constructs the profinite automorphism group of the geometric fibre functor on finite étale covers and its equivalence with finite continuous sets. Its acceptance test is 'Recover the absolute Galois group for Spec K'. The equivalence over Spec K is built twice.
overlaps.proposal: IG.0 owns the general Galois-category equivalence for connected schemes, and its acceptance test for Spec K reuses MC 0D. MC 0D keeps the transport of group objects, homomorphisms and alternating pairings, and may later be re-derived from IG.0. Record one lemma comparing the two normalisations of the fibre functor.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves 7D defines the category of complete local noetherian W(k)-algebras whose residue field is identified with k, the deformation groupoid over it, and the universal deformation over W(k)[[T]]. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1 constructs coefficient categories, with presentations as inverse limits of Artinian quotients, continuous maps from power-series rings and completed tensor products. Both define the same coefficient category C_{W(k)}.
overlaps.proposal: Use one coefficient category: DDPA R03.1 with O = W(k), which already provides the Artinian-quotient and power-series API that 7D's universal property needs. 7D defines the elliptic deformation groupoid over it. If 7D lands first, R03.1 generalises 7D's definition from W(k) to O with a comparison lemma, not a parallel structure.

overlaps.detail: Modular Curves Layer 10 counts the geometric cusps of X_H: m_H of each width 1 and N, counted as orbits of KM 10.6 cusp labels. It also locates the ramification of X₁(N) → X₀(N) over j = 1728 (present iff N ≡ 1 mod 4) and over j = 0 (present iff N ≡ 1 mod 3). ModularForms Layer 10A computes cusp orbits Γ\ℙ¹(ℚ), ε∞ and the elliptic-point counts ε₂ and ε₃ for congruence subgroups on the analytic curve X(Γ). For the prime-level diamond class the same combinatorial counts appear on algebraic and analytic carriers.
overlaps.proposal: Keep both carriers; ModularForms explicitly declines algebraic moduli. Prove the group-theoretic counts for Γ_H (N ≥ 5 prime) once, as a combinatorial lemma on (ℤ/Nℤ)ˣ-orbits and elliptic fixed points, and cite it from both layers. ModularCurvesPartII R12.3 compares the resulting cusp sets.
